name: Markus Brandl
current_role: Co-Founder, Isar Aerospace; current operational role not confirmed (not on the company's current leadership team)
profile: Aerospace engineer who co-founded Isar Aerospace in February 2018 with Daniel Metzler and Josef Fleischmann; all three came out of TUM's WARR student rocketry group, which had built its own engines and a suborbital rocket. Isar's Spectrum rocket reached orbit on 5 Sept 2026 from Andøya, Norway, a first for a commercial company from continental Europe.
interesting_fact: Isar Aerospace's first funding round in summer 2018 came from Viessmann's Vito Ventures, UVC Partners and early SpaceX leader Bulent Altan, who later became Isar's chairman.
notes: Lowest-profile of the three Isar co-founders: not on Isar's current leadership page (CEO Metzler, CTO Araz, CCO Guillen) and not named in recent company releases. Current role unknown. Web-search budget ran out, so no personal profile was found. Isar press office is the only route found.

name: David Carney
current_role: Co-Founder, Chief Strategy Officer and Board Director, Tailscale
profile: Former Google engineer who co-founded Tailscale in 2019 with Avery Pennarun, David Crawshaw and Brad Fitzpatrick. Tailscale builds a WireGuard-based mesh VPN and raised $12M (Series A, 2020), $100M (Series B, 2022) and $160M (Series C led by Accel, April 2025, ~$1.5B valuation). He sits on Tailscale's board alongside CEO Pennarun.
interesting_fact: Tailscale's name was inspired by the 2013 Google research paper 'The Tail at Scale' by Jeff Dean and Luiz André Barroso.
notes: Lower public profile than his co-founders; the strategy/board role suggests he handles go-to-market and partnerships. Web-search budget ran out before a personal deep-cut fact or personal accounts could be found. Route via Tailscale press, or an intro through Pennarun or Fitzpatrick, who are more public.

name: Max Windisch
current_role: Co-Founder and Chief Strategy Officer, Vention (Montreal)
profile: Computer scientist who co-founded Montreal-based Vention with Etienne Lacroix in 2016 to reinvent how manufacturers design, automate and scale. Vention's cloud platform (MachineBuilder, MachineMotion AI) lets factories configure and deploy modular automation and robot cells, and it is expanding into physical AI.
interesting_fact: In Sept 2026 Vention opened a Physical AI lab in Montreal advised by Cohere's Joelle Pineau; physical-AI revenue grew ~400% year over year and the install base spans ~90 Fortune 500 manufacturers.
deep_cut_fact: His career runs through Montreal's 3D-graphics scene: after starting in industrial automation he worked on 2D-3D compositing at Softimage (Microsoft), 3D animation at Kaydara (Autodesk) and early cloud infrastructure at PI/EMC, then went back to automation at GE before Vention.
notes: Low public profile; CEO Etienne Lacroix is the usual spokesperson. His mix of graphics, cloud and automation experience suits a data-center/automation conversation.

name: Qian Qijun (钱其军)
current_role: Chairman, Executive Director and General Manager, Shanghai Cell Therapy Group (上海细胞治疗集团); Dean, Shanghai Cell Therapy Research Institute; Vice Dean, Shanghai University School of Medicine
profile: Chinese oncology and cell-therapy scientist (PhD, professor) who founded Shanghai Cell Therapy Group, which develops CAR-T ('JL-闪CAR-T') and nanobody platforms, gene-writing and nano-delivery systems, cell storage and 'cell rejuvenation' longevity services, and runs the Shanghai Mengchao Cancer Hospital. The group reports 640+ patent applications as of Oct 2026.
interesting_fact: The group frames its mission as a 'longevity revolution' (长寿革命), with the slogan 'Cells For Healthspan'; in Nov 2026 it hosted Nobel chemistry laureate Morten Meldal.
deep_cut_fact: Besides running the company, he founded and directs the Shanghai Wu Mengchao-Nobel Laureates Medical Technology Innovation Center (named for the father of Chinese hepatobiliary surgery), is a National Science Fund for Distinguished Young Scholars recipient, and serves as an editorial adviser to The Lancet.
notes: Matched 'Shanghai Cell' to Shanghai Cell Therapy Group, where 钱其军 is listed as the leading figure and chairman; the company site is Chinese-only. Outreach would need Chinese-language framing; the topic (biotech/longevity) sits outside the podcast's core energy/data-center focus.
